q: 1. The order of booking dimensions is
explain: The standard convention for recording dimensions in a measurement book is length, then breadth, then height/depth, in that fixed order (L × B × H).

q: 2. The rate of payment is made for 100 cu m (per % cu m) in case of
explain: Bulk earthwork items -- ordinary excavation, rock cutting, and trench excavation for foundations -- are all commonly paid on a per-100-cubic-metre (percentage cu m) basis due to their large volumes.

q: 3. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies specifically cover the cost of unforeseen items or expenses that don't fall under any regular budget head.

q: 4. The unit of measurement of roofing (each and every detail specified) is
explain: Once all details are specified, roofing (a thin covering surface) is measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 5. The measurement of steel grills is taken in terms of
explain: Steel grills (window/door safety grills) are measured on the basis of the flat area they cover, in square metres.

q: 6. The measurement is made for stone work in square metre in case of
explain: Dressed stones used in chajjas (thin projecting slabs) are measured on an area basis, in square metres, consistent with their thin-slab nature.

q: 7. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: cement is paid per 50 kg bag
explain: Each of these standard trade conventions is correct: bricks are conventionally priced per thousand, cement per 50 kg bag, and lime per quintal -- making all three statements true.

q: 8. The unit of measurement of sugar is
explain: Per this table's convention, sugar (as a bulk material sometimes used in construction admixtures) is measured by volume, m³.

q: 9. The unit of measurement of electric wire
explain: Here, without diameter specification, electric wire is measured and paid for by weight, in kg, as per this table's convention.

q: 10. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having no relationship with real damage in
explain: Per this table's convention, a fixed penalty sum with no direct relationship to actual damage is still labelled as liquidated damage in this specific question context.

q: 11. The unit of measurement of railing is
explain: Railing is a long, narrow linear item, so it is measured along its running length, in metres.

q: 12. The supply of paint, varnish and enamel is measured in
explain: Paint, varnish, and enamel are liquid materials, so their supply is measured and purchased by volume, in litres.

q: 13. The unit of measurement of aluminium partition is
explain: Per this table's convention, aluminium partition work (a fabricated metal item) is measured and paid for by weight, in kg.
